past_medical_history: Leptomeningeal carcinomatosis concern (breast cancer, treated with lumpectomy + radiation + chemotherapy 6 years ago, currently in clinical remission)

social_history.living_situation: Lives with husband; daughter in same city
social_history.tobacco: Former smoker, 15 pack-years, quit 20 years ago

patient.chief_complaint: Progressive gait deterioration, memory decline, and new urinary incontinence — oncology team concerned about cancer recurrence or leptomeningeal disease
patient.history_present_illness: A 69-year-old retired nurse with breast cancer in clinical remission (6 years post-treatment) was admitted for urgent neurological evaluation of progressive gait deterioration, memory decline, and urinary incontinence over the past 10 months. She was treated with lumpectomy, radiation, and chemotherapy (doxorubicin-cyclophosphamide followed by paclitaxel) 6 years ago and has been in clinical remission on tamoxifen maintenance. Her oncologist and oncology team are alarmed because her symptoms — gait deterioration, cognitive decline, and urinary incontinence — could represent leptomeningeal carcinomatosis (LMC) recurrence, and they have requested urgent neurology consultation. She describes progressive shuffling gait beginning 10 months ago, three falls (no injury), and increasing reliance on a walker. Urinary urgency began approximately 7 months ago, progressing to frank incontinence 2-3 times per week. She describes increasing forgetfulness and difficulty following complex nursing reports she used to review voluntarily. Her oncologist noticed the gait change at a routine visit and was concerned about CNS metastasis or LMC. However, a neurology fellow who examined her noted the gait had a distinctly magnetic quality. A head MRI showed Evans index 0.35 and raised both LMC (leptomeningeal enhancement? — no enhancement present) and NPH as concerns.

neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert, oriented x3. Anxious about cancer recurrence. MoCA 22/30. Mild delayed recall (2/5), executive dysfunction. Normal language. No aphasia.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Normal. No papilledema. No diplopia. No facial numbness. PERRL.
neurological_exam.motor: Normal tone and strength. No focal deficits. No radiculopathic signs.
neurological_exam.sensory: Normal throughout. No dermatomal sensory loss.
neurological_exam.gait: Wide-based, shuffling magnetic gait. Freezing on initiation. TUG 27 seconds. 10-meter walk 21 seconds. Cannot tandem walk. Pull test — 2 steps backward.
neurological_exam.additional: No meningismus. No papilledema. No cranial nerve palsies (would suggest LMC). Bilateral grasp reflexes present (frontal). No skin lesions suggesting metastases.

signal_characteristics.description: No leptomeningeal enhancement on post-contrast T1

mri.impression: 1. Ventriculomegaly with Evans index 0.35. 2. Partial disproportionate sulcal effacement at high convexity (partial DESH pattern). 3. Callosal angle 81 degrees. 4. No leptomeningeal enhancement on post-contrast T1. 5. No parenchymal enhancing lesions. 6. Mild periventricular FLAIR signal. Clinical correlation recommended.

special_tests.flow_cytometry: No abnormal lymphoid or epithelial cell population — negative for malignancy

specialized_test.test_type: High-volume tap trial (40 mL) — after negative CSF cytology confirmed

findings.urinary: No incontinence in 24h post-tap; decreased urgency

specialized_test.impression: Positive tap trial. TUG improved 30% at 24 hours (27 sec to 19 sec); 10-meter walk improved 33% (21 sec to 14 sec); MoCA improved 3 points (22 to 25). No incontinence in 24 hours post-tap; decreased urgency reported. Clinical correlation recommended.

output.proposed: VP shunt surgery in breast cancer survivor on tamoxifen
interactions: Tamoxifen — potent CYP2D6 substrate; no relevant anesthetic interactions
Duloxetine — moderate CYP inhibitor; no significant interaction with anesthesia
warnings: Continue tamoxifen perioperatively — do not hold; interruption risks cancer recurrence
Duloxetine — continue perioperatively; abrupt discontinuation may cause discontinuation syndrome
Routine post-operative DVT prophylaxis is appropriate

output.impression: Negative — sparse-to-no amyloid neuritic plaque density. CL score 9, below the threshold of 24. Clinical correlation recommended.

Mildly hyperdynamic aqueductal flow. Peak velocity 20 cm/s (reference <18 cm/s); stroke volume 70 mcL/cycle (reference <42 mcL/cycle). Both values are above published normative ranges. Clinical correlation recommended.

findings.result: No evidence of breast cancer recurrence. No new mediastinal, pleural, or hepatic lesions. Prior lumpectomy site stable. No skeletal metastases on bone windows.

output.impression: No evidence of systemic malignancy on CT of chest, abdomen, and pelvis. No new mediastinal, pleural, or hepatic lesions. Prior lumpectomy site stable. No skeletal lesions on bone windows. Clinical correlation recommended.

output.query: NPH in cancer survivors differential diagnosis leptomeningeal carcinomatosis CSF cytology

results.title: NPH in cancer survivors — LMC mimicry and diagnostic algorithm
results.key_finding: NPH and LMC can have overlapping features (cognitive decline, incontinence); negative CSF cytology x2 combined with negative post-contrast MRI and positive tap trial effectively excludes LMC

results.title: False-negative CSF cytology in LMC — implications for practice
results.key_finding: Single CSF cytology sensitivity for LMC is 45-60%; three separate cytospin preparations increase sensitivity to >85%; negative x3 with negative MRI strongly excludes LMC

output.summary: Single CSF cytology sensitivity for leptomeningeal carcinomatosis is 45–60%; three separate cytospin preparations increase sensitivity to >85%. Negative CSF cytology combined with negative post-contrast MRI is associated with effective exclusion of leptomeningeal carcinomatosis. Tap trial TUG improvement >20% is associated with VP shunt response in iNPH.

findings.finding: Neurogenic detrusor overactivity — involuntary contractions at 138 mL. No outlet obstruction or stress incontinence.

output.impression: Neurogenic detrusor overactivity. Involuntary contractions at 138 mL. No outlet obstruction or stress incontinence component. Pattern is consistent with detrusor overactivity of neurogenic origin. Clinical correlation recommended.

background.pdr: 9-10 Hz posterior dominant rhythm, symmetric and reactive
background.sleep_features: normal vertex waves and sleep spindles

eeg.impression: Normal awake and drowsy EEG. No epileptiform discharges and no focal slowing.

findings: Normal sinus rhythm. Normal axis and intervals. No acute ST-T changes.

additional_observations: No acute intracranial haemorrhage, established infarct, mass, or midline shift.
Grey-white differentiation preserved; basal cisterns patent.
ct.impression: Non-contrast head CT without acute intracranial abnormality. CT is non-contributory to this evaluation and inferior to MRI for assessing ventricular morphometry (Evans index, callosal angle); clinical correlation with MRI recommended.

No sustained arrhythmia. No pauses greater than 2 seconds. No AV block.

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: Idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus (iNPH) — leptomeningeal carcinomatosis excluded

differential.diagnosis: Vascular cognitive impairment / subcortical ischaemic vascular disease
differential.key_features: Small-vessel disease can produce gait apraxia and executive slowing, but ventriculomegaly out of proportion to white-matter burden and a positive tap test favour NPH
Active malignancy mandates exclusion by CSF cytology and gadolinium-enhanced MRI; iNPH is supported when CSF cytology is negative on adequate sampling
Shuffling gait overlaps, but absence of resting tremor, asymmetric rigidity, or L-dopa response and presence of magnetic gait + DESH favour NPH

Cognitive decline overlaps; AD typically presents with episodic-memory predominance and hippocampal atrophy rather than frontal-subcortical pattern and magnetic gait; CSF biomarkers / amyloid PET resolve copathology

differential.diagnosis: Cerebral atrophy with secondary ex-vacuo ventriculomegaly
differential.key_features: Ventriculomegaly proportionate to sulcal widening, callosal angle >90°, and absence of DESH or transependymal signal argue against true NPH
No history of trauma, SAH, or meningitis on review; would be considered if history suggested antecedent intracranial event

optimal_actions.action: Literature review of iNPH diagnostic criteria and shunt-response predictors
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Relkin 2005 INPH Study Group criteria; Tisell 2011 tap-test predictors; Williams 2016 review

optimal_actions.action: Brain MRI — measure Evans index, callosal angle, assess DESH pattern; exclude mass effect, hydrocephalus from secondary cause, and atrophy
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Ventriculomegaly with Evans index >0.3, DESH pattern (tight high-convexity sulci + widened Sylvian fissures), callosal angle <90°, periventricular transependymal signal; no mass effect or aqueductal obstruction

optimal_actions.action: Reversible-cause labs (TSH, B12, RPR, HIV) to exclude metabolic / infectious dementia mimics
optimal_actions.expected_finding: TSH, B12, RPR, HIV negative or within normal range; reversible mimics excluded

optimal_actions.action: Baseline neuropsychological battery — subcortical/frontal pattern, and reference for pre/post-tap comparison
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Frontal-subcortical pattern: executive dysfunction and slowed processing predominate over episodic amnesia

optimal_actions.action: Large-volume lumbar puncture (30-50 mL tap test) with opening pressure and pre/post gait + neuropsych assessment
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Opening pressure <25 cmH2O (normal); 30-50 mL CSF removed; pre/post tap gait and neuropsych assessment shows objective improvement supporting shunt-responsive iNPH

optimal_actions.action: Neurosurgery consultation for VP shunt candidacy and perioperative planning
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Neurosurgery accepts patient for VP shunt evaluation with programmable valve

optimal_actions.action: Amyloid PET (optional) — screen for AD copathology that may temper cognitive (but not gait) shunt benefit
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Inform shunt prognosis: AD copathology common (~50% iNPH)

useless_tools.rationale: EEG is non-specific for NPH and does not distinguish from neurodegenerative alternatives in this chronic gait/cognitive presentation
ECG is unrelated to the diagnostic workup of chronic gait + cognitive + urinary triad once cardiogenic syncope is not on the differential
Echocardiography does not contribute to NPH evaluation in the absence of syncope or cardioembolic stroke workup
Head CT is inferior to MRI for measuring Evans index and callosal angle and for excluding secondary causes; only justified if MRI is contraindicated
Cardiac monitoring has no diagnostic role in NPH and is reserved for syncope or arrhythmia workup

sequence_constraints.reason: MRI must precede large-volume LP to exclude mass effect or secondary obstructive hydrocephalus before removing 30-50 mL of CSF
Baseline neuropsychological and gait assessment must be obtained before the tap test so that pre/post change can be measured (tap response is the shunt-response predictor)

critical_actions: Obtain brain MRI before lumbar puncture to exclude mass effect or obstructive hydrocephalus
Document objective pre-tap gait (TUG and 10-metre walk) and neuropsychological baseline so that pre/post-tap change can be quantified
Remove 30-50 mL of CSF during the tap test (a low-volume LP under-samples and biases the test toward false negative)
Re-assess gait and cognition 1-4 hours after the tap and again at 24 hours (the response window for tap-test prediction of shunt benefit)
Refer to neurosurgery for VP shunt evaluation when imaging, clinical, and tap-test criteria support iNPH
contraindicated_actions: Do not perform large-volume lumbar puncture before MRI excludes mass effect or obstructive hydrocephalus
Do not infer iNPH from ventriculomegaly alone — DESH, callosal angle <90°, and a clinical triad are required
Do not diagnose Alzheimer's disease in a patient with gait-predominant presentation and ventriculomegaly without first excluding NPH
Do not attribute the syndrome to 'normal ageing' or 'deconditioning' once the imaging criteria for ventriculomegaly are met
Do not commit to iNPH without ruling out leptomeningeal disease by CSF cytology when active or recent malignancy is in the history
key_reasoning_points: iNPH diagnosis (Relkin 2005 INPH Study Group) requires (a) Hakim's triad of gait disturbance, cognitive impairment, and urinary urgency/incontinence — gait is typically first and most prominent; (b) ventriculomegaly with Evans >0.3 and DESH on MRI without mass effect; (c) age >40 and chronic course; (d) opening pressure <25 cmH2O; (e) absence of an alternative explanation
MRI is the imaging modality of choice — measure Evans index and callosal angle (<90° supports NPH) and confirm DESH (tight high-convexity sulci + wide Sylvian fissures)

The tap test is a 30-50 mL large-volume LP with pre/post objective gait (TUG, 10-metre walk) and neuropsychological assessment; opening pressure must be normal (<25 cmH2O) to satisfy the 'normal pressure' criterion
Tap-test sensitivity is only 50-80%; a single negative tap does not exclude NPH — an extended (3-5 day) lumbar drainage trial can resolve borderline cases
Reversible-cause labs (TSH, B12, RPR, HIV) are mandatory before attributing the syndrome to NPH
Approximately 50% of iNPH patients have AD copathology — this lowers cognitive benefit from shunting but does not negate gait benefit
Shunt response is best predicted by an objectively positive tap test or extended drainage trial in a patient who meets imaging and clinical criteria

red_herrings.data_point: Past breast cancer (currently in clinical remission)
red_herrings.intended_effect: The syndrome is presumptively attributed to leptomeningeal carcinomatosis and NPH is not pursued
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Negative CSF cytology on adequate sampling and absence of leptomeningeal enhancement on gadolinium MRI exclude leptomeningeal disease; iNPH remains the operative diagnosis

metadata.difficulty_variant_description: Diagnostic puzzle NPH — breast cancer survivor with Hakim's triad; leptomeningeal carcinomatosis as major red herring requiring comprehensive exclusion (cytology x3, flow cytometry, MRI, staging CT) before NPH diagnosis confirmed.
metadata.difficulty_rationale: 6 required tools (MRI, labs, neuropsych baseline, large-volume LP/tap, neurosurgery consult, literature), 1 grounded red herrings; differential includes 6 active alternatives. Active malignancy mandates parallel exclusion of leptomeningeal disease.
